To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we introduce a novel way to represent RNA-seq data as a graph, (b) we show that this representation is useful to identify RNA classes and (c) we demonstrate that the proposed method is accurate, robust and scalable.
we developed BlockClust, a method to cluster ncRNAs using their expression profiles, and we showed its performance on several data sets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection and classification of noncoding RNAs.
the development of efficient algorithms for the analysis of RNA-seq data, and in particular the analysis of the processing of non-coding RNA.
the detection, characterization and classification of noncoding RNAs (ncRNA).

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce an efficient method to cluster and classify ncRNAs from small RNA-seq data.
we developed BlockClust, a tool to cluster and classify ncRNAs based on their processing pattern, that we show to be accurate, scalable and robust across different species.
we introduce an approach that can be used to identify ncRNA families in a data-driven manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed method is able to identify ncRNA families in a scalable way, and it is robust to different organisms, tissues, cell lines and sequencing technologies.
